EA.name: Expert Adherence (Training)
EA.characteristics: Player matches or cleanly outperforms the expert through the section.  - Standard adherence: the driver line stays close to the expert racing line for the whole range, `expert_time_difference` is stable, and speed delta stays small or returns toward parity.  - A time gap below 200ms is not a mistake by itself. When the preflight time-gap facts show no significant losing-time run and no technical-error evidence, treat the section as clean context, not MSP/RM.  - Expert-or-better clean section: EA can still apply when the player is ahead of the expert, gaining on the expert, or using a cleaner/faster line than the expert reference, even if the line is wider/tighter. Require no off-track/cutting/instability evidence and no MSP / RM / MSR / PS gate.  - Use the current preflight time-gap summaries, but distinguish gap value direction from loss-rate shape. A positive but flat or constant carried time gap only means the player is already behind, not that a new mistake happened inside this range.  - When `expert_time_difference` is absent, do not rule out EA solely because the time-gap gate is unavailable. Use trajectory, speed/brake/throttle samples, segment shape, and the absence of MSP/RM/MSR/PS evidence.Mutually exclusive with MSP and RM.

MSP.name: Mistake (Practice)
MSP.characteristics: Technical driving error causing time loss or instability, NOT caused by interaction with a close opponent.  - MSP / RM boundary is decided by whether a new mistake action or newly worsening loss rate happens inside this split section, not by the section's start iloc or by `expert_time_difference` starting near zero. At lap/session start, near-zero time difference is baseline context only.  - If the section contains the new mistake action (run wide, cut tight, braking / throttle error, instability, or newly worsening time-loss rate), label the section MSP even if the driver later recovers, merges back, or the whole-section loss-rate slope decreases.  - Time-gap evidence must show a new or worsening loss event inside the range. Use the current preflight fact sentences, especially the selected losing run and the gap value versus loss-rate distinction. In raw query output these correspond to fields under `extra` such as `verdict`, `selected_losing_time_run`, `point_trend_runs`, `start_trend`, `overall_point_trend`, `delta_value`, `total_change_direction`, and `slope_shape`.  - A rising time-gap run supports MSP only when it aligns with a new in-section driving error or strengthening loss rate and the absolute gap or gap change is at least 200ms. Mistake time-gap evidence is the opposite of RM: the time gap increased at the end, with a spike or raising in between. Do not infer MSP from a sub-200ms gap, absolute endpoint gap, endpoint delta, `starts_near_zero`, `total_change_direction`, or `delta_value` alone.  - If the graph enters the section already rising, but preflight says the loss rate is decreasing, reversing to recovery, shrinking by the end, or has only a constant carried gap while trajectory/brake/throttle evidence shows merge-back behavior, treat that as RM or empty context rather than new MSP.  - Speed gap is supporting MSP evidence when the `speed_difference` preflight shows repeated value growth or a worsening overall value trend, especially when those ranges align with the new mistake action and the time gap also worsens. Do not decide MSP from one isolated speed sample.  - The driver line exceeds the expert envelope because of a new in-section spike outward (ran wide) or inward (cut tight). Recovery back toward the expert racing line later in the same section does not cancel MSP when the section began with the mistake action, but a range that begins after the mistake and primarily merges back is RM.  - Use RM instead when the section does not contain the new mistake action and the first qualifying action is recovery / merge from an already-carried off-line state, off-track state, instability, or prior incident with the RM time-gap pattern.  - In opponent-capable data, `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)`    does NOT return an adverse racing outcome (`failed_attack` or    `broken_defense`). A close opponent + adverse classifier outcome => MSR.Mutually exclusive with EA, RM, MSR. The detailed-annotation flow refines MSP sub-ranges later; attach MSP at the section level when the section starts with or is dominated by a technical error that occurs inside the section.

MSR.name: Mistake (Racing)
MSR.characteristics: Time / position loss caused by an interaction with a close opponent inside the section.  - Use the preflight `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)` result. Require `outcome` = `failed_attack` or `broken_defense` with medium/high confidence. Low / weak confidence means inspect opponent trajectory or submit an empty label list.  - Use `find_nearest_opponent` / `query_opponent_trajectory` only as supporting evidence for the primary slot and technique.  - `expert_time_difference` may grow across the interaction window, but the opponent classifier outcome is the gate.Mutually exclusive with EA, RM, MSP. No close opponent or classifier outcome not in {failed_attack, broken_defense} => not MSR.

RM.name: Recovery & Merge
RM.characteristics: Player recovering from a prior mistake inside this section.  - RM / MSP boundary is decided by whether the current split section contains the new mistake action. Use RM when the section does not contain the new mistake action and the first qualifying behavior is recovery / merge from an already-carried off-line state, off-track state, instability, prior incident, or already-rising expert-time gap.  - A preceding mistake/off-track/incident explains why recovery is needed. An `expert_time_difference` trace that enters the range already rising is evidence that time loss may have begun before this section; do not treat that incoming positive slope as a new in-section MSP by itself. A near-zero starting value is also not MSP evidence by itself, especially at lap/session start.  - Time-gap recovery evidence should come from the current preflight summaries, especially selected recovering runs, value movement toward zero, and loss-rate easing. In raw query output, use `extra.selected_recovery_run`, `extra.point_trend_runs`, `extra.start_trend`, `extra.overall_point_trend`, `extra.slope_shape`, and `extra.near_zero_summary.moves_toward_zero`.  - the time gap must be lower at the end, or the time gap can be higher at the end but the ending slope has to be lower than the starting slope and there is no spike or raising in the middle.  - RM can still start with a rising time gap when the action evidence is recovery / merge and the end-of-range facts show shrinking, reversal to recovery, movement toward zero, or a decreasing loss rate with no spike or raising in the middle. Do not classify RM from speed alone if the time gap keeps worsening through the end.  - Speed gap is supporting RM evidence when `speed_difference` stops widening, narrows, or moves toward parity during the merge-back phase, matching the time-gap recovery facts.  - The driver line trends back toward the expert racing line from a non-zero or already-compromised state, with brake/throttle action consistent with rejoining or merging back.Do NOT use RM just because an MSP section has a later recovery phase; if the section starts with a mistake action that occurs in this section, the whole parent segment is MSP and recovery is described in the reasoning or detailed child sub-segment. Do NOT attach when the player started clean with no carried mistake/off-line state; that is EA or an empty parent, not RM. Mutually exclusive with EA and MSP.

PS.name: Pit Stop
PS.characteristics: Player is in the circuit's Pit section. Pit procedure is PS even when the car is accelerating out and returning toward the racing surface.  - Require pit evidence from the preflight `locate_circuit_section` result, splitter context, or top match that overlaps the circuit's known Pit section.  - When `locate_circuit_section` is ambiguous between Pit and the adjacent straight because they share a normalized range, sustained pit-lane-style trajectory offset plus large player/expert speed separation or slow pit-exit acceleration is sufficient Pit-section procedure evidence.  - Do not label PS from speed rise, low speed, trajectory offset, or acceleration back toward track speed alone when the range is in a normal racing section away from Pit.Compatible with the circuit label. Do NOT combine with EA / MSP / MSR / O / OD.

O.name: Successful Overtake
O.characteristics: Player gained a position on a specific opponent inside the section. Multi-car positional data (`Car_{1..60}_pos_{x,y,z}`) is the gate.  - Use the preflight `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)` result. Require `outcome: pass_completed` with medium/high confidence; the deterministic signed longitudinal relationship says the opponent was ahead at entry and behind by exit. Empty / no-data / non-pass outcomes => do NOT attach O. Low / weak confidence means inspect opponent trajectory or submit an empty label list.  - Player-trace evidence can explain technique: late-brake signature past the expert reference, sustained outside / inside line deviation not explained by MSP / RM, or speed greater than expert on equal-or-less throttle.A close opponent + failed attack is MSR at the section level; sub-labelled `MSR1` in the detailed flow. A successful defense is OD, not O.

OD.name: Successful Defense
OD.characteristics: Player held position against a real, close opponent inside the section.  - Use the preflight `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)` result. Require `outcome: held_defense` with medium/high confidence; the deterministic relationship says the opponent threatened from behind / alongside but did not get ahead by exit. A merely close car with no held-defense outcome is not OD. Low / weak confidence means inspect opponent trajectory or submit an empty label list.  - Player-trace evidence can explain technique: earlier braking than expert, tighter trajectory than expert for inside cover, or a throttle lift on a straight with no brake onset for defensive lift. Time delta may grow briefly during the defense as long as position holds.A defense that failed (opponent got past) is MSR at the section level; sub-labelled `MSR2` in the detailed flow.

prompt_rules.required_behavior_parent_label_rule: Every saved lap segment must include at least one behavior parent label from {{eligible_behavior_labels}}.If no required behavior parent label fits the whole split-section range, submit an empty label_ids array to drop the range instead of saving a parentless segment.

mode_exclusion_rules.practice: Pick at most one technical/recovery behavior parent from {MSP, RM}; MSP + RM is a contradiction. PS should not be combined with MSP.
mode_exclusion_rules.racing: Pick at most one opponent-aware behavior parent from {O, OD, MSR}; O + OD, O + MSR, and OD + MSR are contradictions. PS is allowed only for Pit-section procedure and should not be combined with O / OD / MSR.

interaction_focus.body: This split range {{origin}}. For this work unit, identify the target car from the splitter evidence first, then do ONLY overtake offence / defense annotation: pick O for a successful attacking pass, OD for a held defense, or MSR for a failed attack / broken defense. If the opponent evidence is only close-following/draft context, or the opponent stays tucked directly behind without a lateral/alongside threat, submit `label_ids: []` rather than labeling normal practice-driving telemetry such as EA / MSP / RM. PS is still valid when the range has Pit-section procedure evidence.

prompt_rules.task_intro: Annotate ONE lap range. The deterministic splitter handed you a fixed split-section boundary; if this is an opponent interaction window, the boundary is event-shaped and circuit sections are context only. Your job is to include the circuit id and one selected circuit_section id from splitter or preflight context, at least one required behavior parent label for any saved segment, optional lap-parent-allowed segment-type labels, and an optional matching sub-label.
prompt_rules.splitter_section_context: Splitter context: `{{circuit_id}}` ({{circuit_name}}), `{{section_id}}` ({{section_name}}). Use this as the selected circuit_section unless Pit-section evidence makes the Pit section the better knowledge-base fit. If `locate_circuit_section` is ambiguous, use `top_matches` only as competing evidence to resolve to one circuit_section id.
prompt_rules.preselected_section_context: Splitter section context: `{{preselected_section_id}}` ({{preselected_section_name}}) from the opponent sub-segment; include it in `label_ids`.
selection_notes: Preflight semantic label candidates cover behavior, segment-type, and sub-label choices.
When any main-label, segment-type, or sub-label signature fits only part of the range, omit that label or submit an empty `label_ids` array to drop the range.

payload_shape.intro: `payload_json` must be a JSON object of this shape:
payload_shape.reasoning_placeholder: <4-6 sentence human-readable evidence note citing ilocs, values, trends, tool verdicts, range-fit rationale, and any ambiguous option rejected>
followup: `label_ids` carries the circuit id, one selected circuit_section id, and your main / segment-type / sub picks together. Every saved segment must contain at least one of {{eligible_behavior_labels}}; otherwise submit an empty `label_ids` array as the valid 'drop this section' signal. The runner reports back the split section range.

hard_rules: Do not invent label IDs; circuit / circuit_section ids must come from splitter or preflight context, every other id from preflight semantic candidates.

When `locate_circuit_section` reports ambiguity, choose exactly one circuit_section id using splitter context and behavior evidence. For Pit-vs-straight ties, choose Pit when Pit-section evidence supports pit procedure; otherwise choose the normal racing-surface section. A Pit-vs-adjacent-straight ambiguity plus sustained pit-lane-style trajectory offset and large player/expert speed separation or slow pit-exit acceleration counts as Pit-section procedure evidence. Do not include multiple same-range circuit_section ids.
prompt_rules.whole_range_label_rule: Every behavior, segment-type, and sub-label must describe the final annotation range as a whole. Do not attach a label because it matches only one phase, one apex moment, or a short slice inside the range; omit that label or leave it for detailed child sub-segment annotation.
prompt_rules.segment_action_model_rule: Evaluate the saved lap parent segment as a complete action group over the final iloc range. Driver/expert turning / trajectory, brake, and throttle comparison is required for segment completeness at entry or exit; do not treat complete action-group evidence as optional sub-label evidence.
prompt_rules.reasoning_note_rule: Write `reasoning` as a longer human annotation note: 4-6 concise sentences covering the final iloc range, selected label fit, key telemetry values or trends, deterministic tool verdicts, and why competing labels were omitted. When two plausible labels or circuit sections are ambiguous, name the option that was not selected and state why it was rejected. For time-delta prose, say `losing time run` and avoid ranking/adjective phrasing.
